sn22.55:1.2: There the Blessed One uttered this inspired utterance:
sn22.55:1.3: “‘It might not be, and it might not be for me; it will not be, and it will not be for me’:
sn22.55:1.4: resolving thus, a bhikkhu can cut off the lower fetters.”
sn22.55:1.5: When this was said, a certain bhikkhu said to the Blessed One:
sn22.55:1.7: can a bhikkhu, resolving thus: ‘It might not be, and it might not be for me; it will not be, and it will not be for me,’ cut off the lower fetters?”
sn22.55:2.1: “Here, bhikkhu, the uninstructed worldling, who is not a seer of the noble ones …
sn22.55:3.1: “He does not understand as it really is impermanent form as ‘impermanent form’ …
sn22.55:3.4: impermanent volitional formations as ‘impermanent volitional formations’ …
sn22.55:4.1: “He does not understand as it really is painful form as ‘painful form’ …
sn22.55:4.4: painful volitional formations as ‘painful volitional formations’ …
sn22.55:5.1: “He does not understand as it really is selfless form as ‘selfless form’ …
sn22.55:5.4: selfless volitional formations as ‘selfless volitional formations’ …
sn22.55:6.1: “He does not understand as it really is conditioned form as ‘conditioned form’ …
sn22.55:6.4: conditioned volitional formations as ‘conditioned volitional formations’ …
sn22.55:6.6: “He does not understand as it really is: ‘Form will be exterminated’ …
sn22.55:7.1: “The instructed noble disciple, bhikkhu, who is a seer of the noble ones …
sn22.55:7.2: does not regard form as self …
sn22.55:8.1: “He understands as it really is impermanent form as ‘impermanent form’ …
sn22.55:8.6: “He understands as it really is painful form as ‘painful form’ … painful consciousness as ‘painful consciousness.’
sn22.55:8.7: “He understands as it really is selfless form as ‘selfless form’ … selfless consciousness as ‘selfless consciousness.’
sn22.55:8.8: “He understands as it really is conditioned form as ‘conditioned form’ … conditioned consciousness as ‘conditioned consciousness. ’
sn22.55:8.9: “He understands as it really is: ‘Form will be exterminated’ …
sn22.55:9.1: “With the extermination of form, feeling, perception, volitional formations, and consciousness, that bhikkhu,
sn22.55:9.3: resolving thus: ‘It might not be, and it might not be for me; it will not be, and it will not be for me,’ can cut off the lower fetters.”
sn22.55:9.4: “Resolving thus, venerable sir, a bhikkhu can cut off the lower fetters.
sn22.55:10.1: But how should one know, how should one see, for the immediate destruction of the taints to occur?”
sn22.55:10.2: “Here, bhikkhu, the uninstructed worldling becomes frightened over an unfrightening matter. For this is frightening to the uninstructed worldling:
sn22.55:10.3: ‘It might not be, and it might not be for me;
sn22.55:10.4: it will not be, and it will not be for me.’
sn22.55:11.1: But the instructed noble disciple does not become frightened over an unfrightening matter. For this is not frightening to the noble disciple:
sn22.55:11.2: ‘It might not be, and it might not be for me;
sn22.55:11.3: it will not be, and it will not be for me.’
sn22.55:11.4: “Consciousness, bhikkhu, while standing, might stand engaged with form …
sn22.55:11.7: engaged with volitional formations; based upon volitional formations, established upon volitional formations, with a sprinkling of delight, it might come to growth, increase, and expansion.
sn22.55:12.2: ‘Apart from form, apart from feeling, apart from perception, apart from volitional formations, I will make known the coming and going of consciousness, its passing away and rebirth, its growth, increase, and expansion’—that is impossible.
sn22.55:13.1: “Bhikkhu, if a bhikkhu has abandoned lust for the form element, with the abandoning of lust the basis is cut off: there is no support for the establishing of consciousness.
sn22.55:13.2: If he has abandoned lust for the feeling element …
sn22.55:13.5: for the consciousness element, with the abandoning of lust the basis is cut off: there is no support for the establishing of consciousness.
sn22.55:13.6: “When that consciousness is unestablished, not coming to growth, nongenerative, it is liberated.
sn22.55:13.7: By being liberated, it is steady; by being steady, it is content; by being content, he is not agitated. Being unagitated, he personally attains Nibbāna.
sn22.55:13.8: He understands: ‘Destroyed is birth, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being.’
sn22.55:13.9: “It is, bhikkhu, for one who knows thus, for one who sees thus, that the immediate destruction of the taints occurs.”
